source.author: cic
source.text: qui vere falsone, quaerere mittimusdicitur oculis se privasse; certe, ut quam minime animus a cogitationibus abduceretur, patrimonium neglexit, agros deseruit incultos, quid quaerens aliud nisi vitam beatam?
source.text_original: qui —vere falsone, quaerere mittimus—dicitur oculis se privasse; certe, ut quam minime animus a cogitationibus abduceretur, patrimonium neglexit, agros deseruit incultos, quid quaerens aliud nisi vitam beatam?
source.text_english: He is said to have deprived himself of his eyes; at any rate, in order that his mind might be drawn away as little as possible from thoughts, he neglected his property, left his fields untilled. What was he seeking other than a happy life?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: denique quosdam etiam mundi philosophos legimus, ut totam cogitationem ad mentis cogerent puritatem, sibi oculos eruisse.
reuse.text_original: denique quosdam etiam mundi philosophos legimus, ut totam cogitationem ad mentis cogerent puritatem, sibi oculos eruisse.
reuse.text_english: Finally, we have even read of certain philosophers of the world who, in order to compel all their thought to the purity of the mind, gouged out their own eyes.
